plots.address: 10052 W Cave Loop, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
plots.notes: 2.1-acre wooded interior lot in West Cave Estates (Travis County, Lake Travis ISD), listed March 3, 2026. Deed allows up to 3 horses. plots.notes: 2-acre cul-de-sac lot in Creek Road Ranch, Dripping Springs (Hays County), across from Camp Lucy. Underground utilities (electric, phone, water available), $1,000/yr HOA with trails and common grounds access. At $182.5k/ac, Scenario A (~$1.635M build within $2M cap).
plots.risks: Level terrain with few trees is a significant MCM site-profile weakness — limits natural slope for walkouts/terracing and provides minimal shade. HOA $1,000/yr — verify CC&Rs for MCM compatibility (flat roof, large glazing). Onion Creek proximity — run FEMA floodplain check on build pad. Small acreage (2 ac) limits siting flexibility. Septic needed.

plots.address: 1008 Bell Springs Rd, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
plots.notes: 5.01-acre flag lot in River Oaks Ranch with city water, electricity, and installed septic already in place — one of the rare fully de-risked utility profiles in Dripping Springs. Many mature trees, long-range Hill Country views, seasonal creek at headwaters of Hamilton Creek. $126.7k/ac. Scenario A (~$1.36M build remaining).
plots.risks: High DOM (~230+ days since Feb 2026 listing) warrants a buildability/access check before advancing — flag lots can have road-frontage or easement constraints. Standard Dripping Springs aquifer recharge-zone and WUI checks required. Confirm city water claim per parcel (not all River Oaks Ranch lots have it).

plots.notes: 2.3-acre wooded lot in the gated Mountain Crest community: native hardwoods including large live oaks, wet-weather creek along the back, multiple cleared build sites, community water + electricity both available (rare for Wimberley — removes both utility unknowns). $97.8k/ac is among the lowest $/acre Wimberley entries in the feed. $120/yr HOA. Scenario A (~$1.77M build remaining).
plots.risks: Smaller acreage (2.3 ac) limits siting freedom vs. ideal Hill Country 5+ ac. Review HOA CC&Rs for MCM compatibility (flat roof, large glazing, modern massing). Wet-weather creek warrants Wimberley-standard floodplain/Atlas-14 build-pad check. WUI and aquifer recharge assessments still required. Commute ~50-60 min downtown.

plots.notes: Cedar-cleared 10-acre parcel revealing mature live oaks, post oaks, and cedar elms throughout — gently rolling terrain with multiple build sites and long-range Hill Country views. 400+ ft paved frontage on Prochnow Rd. Agricultural exemption active (near-zero taxes during design-build). No HOA, light restrictions (MCM-friendly). Neighboring well <500 ft away yielded 35 GPM — strong groundwater indicator for this corridor. Hays County unincorporated (lightest permitting path for unconventional MCM design). Scenario A (~$1.36M build budget remaining at $639k land price).
plots.risks: Standard Dripping Springs flags: Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone check (TCEQ) required before offer — impervious-cover limits apply if parcel is in recharge zone. Verify FEMA floodplain status on intended build pad. Well cost and depth unknown until drilled; 35 GPM nearby well is encouraging but not a guarantee. WUI wildfire exposure: verify Texas A&M Forest Service rating.

plots.notes: 5.16 acres of Texas Hill Country nestled between Wimberley and Dripping Springs in Hays County unincorporated. Heritage Oak trees throughout; panoramic views. Lot sits between Rolling Oaks Drive and Lonesome Trail — dual road frontage allows entrance from either side. No builder timeline or minimum square footage restrictions. Wimberley ISD. $82.4k/ac, Scenario A (~$1.58M build budget remaining).
plots.risks: Well + septic required (standard for Driftwood rural). Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone check (TCEQ) required — Driftwood varies parcel to parcel; impervious-cover limits apply if in recharge zone. CC&Rs for this subdivision not reviewed — must verify no MCM design restrictions (flat roofs, large glazing) before advancing. FEMA floodplain status for build pad unconfirmed. WUI wildfire assessment needed.

plots.address: 2251 W Fitzhugh Rd, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
plots.notes: 2.42-acre parcel in Medlin Creek subdivision (same ranch as 150 Barton Bnd in this feed). Rolling hills ~10 min from downtown Dripping Springs. Electric at road; well + septic required. Seller is builder offering build-to-suit OR buyer may bring own builder — MCM-compatible. HOA $675/yr with no ARB indicated. DSISD. At $299k (~$124k/ac), Scenario A (~$1.70M build budget remaining).
plots.risks: Medlin Creek CC&Rs not reviewed — verify no MCM design restrictions (flat roof, large glazing) before offer. Well + septic required. Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone check (TCEQ) required — impervious-cover limits if parcel falls in recharge zone. FEMA floodplain status for build pad unconfirmed. Long DOM (~134 days as of listing date 2026-05-27) — investigate reason before advancing. At 2.42 ac, smaller than ideal Hill Country minimum.

plots.address: 1250 Myers Creek Rd, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
plots.notes: 7.29-acre parcel in Bell Spring Ranches, densely wooded with mature hardwoods including live oaks. Natural spring with seasonal creek at back of property; 1,158 ft elevation with 'breathtaking views' and 'vibrant Texas sunsets.' Newly-cut driveway path to building site. Annual HOA for common area maintenance only — no ARB indicated. DSISD. $15k recent price reduction. At $435k (~$60k/ac), Scenario A (~$1.56M build budget remaining).
plots.risks: Very long DOM (~300 days) — investigate before advancing: likely creek floodplain, rough access, or obsolete pricing. Seasonal creek + natural dam at back = FEMA 100-yr floodplain check essential for build pad. Newly-cut driveway suggests access was recently cleared — verify paved road frontage to build pad. Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone check (TCEQ) required. Well + septic needed (no utility info in listing). Bell Spring Ranches CC&Rs not reviewed. WUI wildfire assessment needed.

plots.notes: 5.01-acre gated homesite in The Bluffs at Round Mountain, Blanco County. Same subdivision as two other Bluffs lots already in feed ($218k and $250k) — this is the third Bluffs lot now tracked. Wildlife exemption (Blackbuck Antelope) keeps carry cost near zero; property taxes ~$851/yr confirmed. Underground utilities pre-installed — rare for Round Mountain, removes a major build unknown. Paved road access, gated entry. Johnson City ISD. ~40 min to Austin (shorter commute than most Round Mountain entries). At $274,900 (~$54.9k/ac), priced above the $218k and $250k Bluffs lots already in feed but still competitive for a utilities-included Blanco County parcel. Scenario A (~$1.73M build budget remaining).
plots.risks: The Bluffs at Round Mountain HOA/ARB: deed restrictions and architectural guidelines not confirmed — must verify CC&Rs explicitly permit flat roofs, large glazing, and MCM massing before advancing (hard dealbreaker if conservative ARB). At $274,900 this is a meaningful premium over the $218k and $250k Bluffs lots already in the feed — assess whether site characteristics justify the difference vs. advancing an existing Bluffs entry. Well required (underground utilities pre-installed but water source must be confirmed — verify community vs. individual well). Septic required. Blanco County typically limestone (MCM-positive) but verify geotech before offer. 60–70 min commute when Austin traffic is heavy.
plots.utilities: Underground utilities pre-installed; individual well required (verify community vs. individual)

Electric service point location and well-drill cost unknown — buyer must independently verify utility access. Standard Dripping Springs Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone check (TCEQ) and WUI check (TAMFS) required before offer.

Price cut from $750k to $700k in July 2026.

plots.notes: 7.43 acres in Spicewood (Burnet County) with multiple level building sites and rolling Hill Country terrain. Lake Travis ISD. At $420k ($56.5k/ac) this is strong Spicewood value relative to competing listings. Listed June 2026; no HOA indicated.
plots.risks: Listing detail is sparse — utilities (electric proximity, well, septic feasibility) not confirmed. Road type (public paved vs. private easement) needs verification. Burnet County Edwards/Trinity aquifer, FEMA floodplain, and WUI checks all required before advancing.

plots.notes: 8.6 acres in Spicewood with ~680 feet of Red Bluff Creek frontage running toward Lake Travis plus a seasonal creek feeding a small pond — strong creek-and-view landscape. No HOA, no deed restrictions. Listed June 26, 2026 at $550k by Keller Williams Lake Travis.

plots.notes: 5.45-acre Sycamore Creek-front parcel in Longview II subdivision (DSISD, Hays County). Multiple level building sites with gentle slopes and medium trees. Listed Dec 2, 2025; verify active status (~10 months on market).
